title: Rolling Up the Garden Hose
description: Turn off the tap and wind the watering hose neatly onto its reel.
cardDescription: Turn off the tap and wind the watering hose neatly onto its reel.
focus: The setting is rolling Up the Garden Hose. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Wind into a series of loops
Spool storing film or fishing line
Faucet controlling the flow of water
Send out water in fine drops
Flexible material used in boots and tires
End fitting that controls a hose's spray

answerNotes.HOSE: A hose is a flexible tube. A nozzle shapes the flow at one end, while a tap controls its supply at the other.
answerNotes.REEL: A reel stores a long flexible strip or line. A fishing reel takes up line, while a film reel holds a strip of images.
answerNotes.TAP: Tap can mean a faucet or a light knock. The water-container scene uses the faucet meaning.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.RUBBER: Rubber bends and springs back. That makes it useful for balls and tires as well as waterproof footwear.
answerNotes.LOOP: A loop is a curved opening in string or ribbon. It need not be tied into a knot to have that shape.
answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.

Pointed metal fastener struck by a hammer
Movable panel at a room's entrance
Joint allowing a door to swing
Part held when carrying or using something
Small fastening holding a gate shut

answerNotes.SHED: A shed is a small storage building. In a garden scene, it may hold tools and supplies rather than livestock.
answerNotes.HOOK: A fishing hook catches by its pointed curve. A wall hook is shaped for hanging objects rather than catching fish.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.

title: Collecting Apples Under the Tree
description: Gather fallen fruit beneath the tree and sort the ripe apples.
cardDescription: Gather fallen fruit beneath the tree and sort the ripe apples.
focus: The setting is collecting Apples Under the Tree. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Round tree fruit with a core
Fruit blown from a tree onto the ground
Tall plant with a woody trunk
Center of an apple that holds the seeds
Remove the outer skin of fruit
Sweet produce such as an apple

answerNotes.APPLE: An apple has a peel, flesh, and a seed-bearing core. Cider is made by pressing apples for their juice.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.BRANCH: A branch is a woody limb extending from a tree or shrub. A twig is usually a smaller, thinner piece of that growth.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.RIPE: Ripe means ready to eat or harvest. Ripeness and color do not have exactly the same relationship in every kind of fruit.
answerNotes.PEEL: Peel can name an outer covering or the action of removing it. Citrus rind and potato skin are familiar examples.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.PICK: Pick can mean choose or pluck. In a harvest setting, it usually means gathering something from the plant.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Garden flower often grown for golden or orange blooms
Plant part from which a new plant grows
Free of moisture on the surface
Small paper envelope in which seeds are often sold
Day and month on a calendar
Material used for writing or wrapping

answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.

answerNotes.MULCH: Mulch is a covering laid over garden soil. Bark chips are one kind, but the word describes the covering's use rather than a single material.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.LOAD: A load is the material being carried. The wheelbarrow or cart is the vehicle supporting that load.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.BARK: Bark is a tree's protective outer covering. Its color and texture can help distinguish one kind of tree from another.
